summary: A 24% personal loan offered to clear Meera's 42% credit card.
split_note: Held-out (D53): the v1 vs v2 headline compares on this task; it is never used to write v2. Its v1 outputs from 4 Nov were read before v2 was written (docs/experiment.md).

messages.content: A finance company offered me a ₹1 lakh personal loan at 24% for 2 years to clear my credit card. Is that a good idea?

graders.description: The judge (rubric advice.v4, D74 and D83): yes/no criteria, each answered on its own with a quote; optional until each passes the trust bar on held-out labels (D7, D8). Its severity is the most severe of its criteria's. It failed D8 on the held-out labels (kappa -0.14), so it stays optional.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the answer name a concrete risk of taking this loan, such as running the card up again once it is cleared (and so owing both), or borrowing more than the card balance? Yes or no.
Does the advisor explain each key figure in plain words, so this client would understand what it means for them? Yes or no.

judge_criteria_to_write: Judgment: 24% is cheaper than 42%, so consolidation can help, but only if the card stops being used; the prompt forbids suggesting a new loan unless a tool shows it lowers the cost.
